lines.text: Could we fit in one city? All eight billion, with room to breathe.
lines.phonemes: kʊd wiː fˈɪt ɪn wˈʌn sˈɪɾi? ˈɔːl ˈeɪt bˈɪliən, wɪð ɹˈuːm tə bɹˈiːð.

lines.text: There are a lot of us, and it can feel like the world is full. So give each person half a square meter, the room a calm crowd keeps.
lines.phonemes: ðɛɹˌɑːɹ ɐ lˈɑːt ʌv ˌʌs, ænd ɪt kæn fˈiːl lˈaɪk ðə wˈɜːld ɪz fˈʊl. sˌoʊ ɡˈɪv ˈiːtʃ pˈɜːsən hˈæf ɐ skwˈɛɹ mˈiːɾɚ, ðə ɹˈuːm ɐ kˈɑːm kɹˈaʊd kˈiːps.

lines.text: Now bring everyone in, and the crowd keeps spreading, street after street, until it settles into a square you could drive across in under an hour.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ bɹˈɪŋ ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn ˈɪn, ænd ðə kɹˈaʊd kˈiːps spɹˈɛdɪŋ, stɹˈiːt ˈæftɚ stɹˈiːt, ʌntˈɪl ɪt sˈɛɾəlz ˌɪntʊ ɐ skwˈɛɹ juː kʊd dɹˈaɪv əkɹˌɑːs ɪn ˌʌndɚɹ ɐn ˈaʊɚ.

lines.text: You could squeeze us tighter, but packed twice as close, a crowd starts to move like a fluid, and that's when it turns dangerous. So we keep the room, and all of humanity still covers just two or three Londons.
lines.phonemes: juː kʊd skwˈiːz ˌʌs tˈaɪɾɚ, bˌʌt pˈækt twˈaɪs æz klˈoʊs, ɐ kɹˈaʊd stˈɑːɹts tə mˈuːv lˈaɪk ɐ flˈuːɪd, ænd ðæts wɛn ɪt tˈɜːnz dˈeɪndʒɚɹəs. sˌoʊ wiː kˈiːp ðə ɹˈuːm, ænd ˈɔːl ʌv hjuːmˈænᵻɾi stˈɪl kˈʌvɚz dʒˈʌst tˈuː ɔːɹ θɹˈiː lˈʌndənz.

lines.text: From orbit, you'd struggle to find us. And packed like water, every body would fit in a cube a little shorter than the world's tallest tower.
lines.phonemes: fɹʌm ˈɔːɹbɪt, juːd stɹˈʌɡəl tə fˈaɪnd ˌʌs. ænd pˈækt lˈaɪk wˈɔːɾɚ, ˈɛvɹi bˈɑːdi wʊd fˈɪt ɪn ɐ kjˈuːb ɐ lˈɪɾəl ʃˈɔːɹɾɚ ðɐn ðə wˈɜːldz tˈɔːlɪst tˈaʊɚ.

lines.text: Nudge how dense we are either way, and that cube barely changes size.
lines.phonemes: nˈʌdʒ hˌaʊ dˈɛns wiː ɑːɹ ˈiːðɚ wˈeɪ, ænd ðæt kjˈuːb bˈɛɹli tʃˈeɪndʒᵻz sˈaɪz.

lines.text: So the world isn't full. It only feels that way from inside a city.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ ðə wˈɜːld ˌɪzənt fˈʊl. ɪɾ ˈoʊnli fˈiːlz ðæt wˈeɪ fɹʌm ɪnsˈaɪd ɐ sˈɪɾi.
